body.evidence: Champion telemetry: dev primary plateaus at 0.6017 by epoch 7 while train loss keeps falling and the train/dev gap grows 0.033 -> 0.130 monotonically. The model keeps learning something (loss down, train primary up) that does not transfer to within-user ordering — a signature of objective/metric mismatch rather than pure capacity overfitting. The seed contract text also explicitly flags that no ranking-aligned loss exists in this tree, so this direction is entirely unmeasured here.
body.hypothesis: Replacing the pointwise logloss with a within-user pairwise BPR objective (sample positive/negative impression pairs from the SAME user_id) raises the primary metric by ~0.01-0.02, because the metric averages AUC and nDCG@5 inside each user while pointwise logloss spends most of its capacity fitting the global/user-level click rate, which is exactly the component the metric quotients out.
body.mechanism: Add `step_pairwise(Xp, Xn)` to model.py: forward both rows, g = -sigmoid(-(z_p - z_n))/B applied with +g on the positive row and -g on the negative row through the shared `_apply` path (call `_apply` once on the stacked pair matrix with signed coefficients so Adam sees one update). In train.py, precompute per-user positive and negative index lists with `group_bounds`, then each epoch sample B pairs (one positive, one uniformly drawn negative from the same user, users with only one class skipped). Early stopping, checkpointing and the train_subset return path are untouched. config.json gains loss='pairwise' and pairs_per_epoch.

reflection.next_question: Given the objective is not binding, does the ceiling move when feature coverage does? The single highest-value remaining probe is whether the FM is starved of signal rather than mis-trained: add the interaction/context columns the baseline drops (exposed via data.columns, plus the harness-computed dur_bucket edges the contract text explicitly flags as reachable but unused) on top of the BPR base, which has the larger overfitting headroom (gap 0.058 vs 0.085). If features also fail to move dev primary past ~0.604, the remaining gap to the 0.848 oracle is a model-class limit (FM 2nd-order is too weak) and the last effort should go to a GBDT ranker (lightgbm lambdarank, grouped by user_id) rather than to further FM tuning.
reflection.prediction_comment: Directionally right, magnitude wrong by ~50x: expected +0.015, observed +0.000296. Treat this as the first calibration point and shrink the prior on 'reformulate the loss' proposals in this tree hard. The hypothesis was well-specified and pre-registered a numeric bar (0.6060) that it missed, so the negative is decisive rather than ambiguous.
reflection.remaining_uncertainty: Cannot separate 'ranking losses are useless here' from 'BPR with uniform in-user negatives is too weak a ranking loss'. A lambda-weighted or nDCG-aware pairing (weighting pairs by their position swap gain) attacks nDCG@5 specifically, and nDCG@5 was the component that got slightly WORSE here — so the listwise family is not 100% closed. It is, however, closed at the magnitude that matters. Also unresolved: whether the smaller gap means BPR would be a better base for a higher-capacity model (more factors / more features), since it has more headroom before overfitting — that is a joint hypothesis this run cannot test with 1 evaluation left.
reflection.what_happened: The pairwise BPR objective ran cleanly (pairwise telemetry: 24,290 usable users, 382,579 positives, 570,556 pairs/epoch, 9 epochs, 16.6s fit) and produced a signed dev primary of 0.601992 versus the champion's 0.601696 — a delta of +0.000296, roughly 1/50th of the predicted +0.015 and well short of the pre-registered success bar of 0.6060. Component metrics moved in opposite directions (GAUC 0.667382 -> 0.668076, nDCG@5 0.536011 -> 0.535907), i.e. essentially a wash. The one real structural change is the train/dev gap: 0.0580 at the selected epoch versus 0.0852 for the pointwise champion, and the dev curve still peaks and turns over by epoch 5 while train primary climbs monotonically to 0.702.
reflection.why: The mechanism was implemented and did what it claimed — the loss is genuinely within-user pairwise, the gradient sign is evidently correct (train loss falls 0.660 -> 0.507, train primary rises monotonically, dev primary rises then plateaus rather than collapsing), and the pairwise-specific counters confirm same-user sampling with single-class users skipped. So this is a clean test of the hypothesis, not a broken implementation. But the causal claim behind it is refuted: removing the 'capacity spent on global/user-level click rate' bought +0.0003, which is inside the ~0.0008 seed sigma implied by epsilon=0.002 being 2.5 sigma. The predicted channel does not exist at the size claimed.
